A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 24-page work, including Appendices A–L. Text and rendered pages match throughout, except for the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its self-link.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments and Mapper analyses on MD-Offense, including classification results, topological metrics, sensitivity tests, and cross-model comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, including Tables 1, 3, and 7.

M1.justification: The embedding extraction, Mapper filtering/covering/clustering procedure, lens functions, and HDBSCAN components are identical in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use MD-Offense for English offensive-language classification, with the same three topical domains and A0, A+, and A++ agreement groups (Section 4.1 and Appendix A).

E2.justification: Tables 3 and 7 retain the same six models: BERT-Base, DeBERTa-Base, DistilBERT, E5-Base, MiniLM, and RoBERTa-Large. The pretrained-versus-fine-tuned and lens comparisons also retain the same participants.

E3.justification: Splits, metrics, and experimental settings are unchanged, including three training epochs, batch size 8, learning rate 2e-5, and Mapper resolution/overlap settings of 40/0.3 for 1D lenses and 20/0.2 for 2D lenses.

E4.justification: Appendices D–L retain the same resolution and overlap sensitivity tests, noise-exclusion analysis, per-lens analyses, qualitative examples, and robustness checks across lens dimensionalities and models.

E5.justification: Both report three-seed averaging in Appendix B and the same across-lens means, standard deviations, and error bars in Table 1, Figure 6, and Appendix L. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting changes occur.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 1 retains A0 values of 98.0 ± 2.4% for components exceeding 90% prediction purity and 77.7 ± 20.5% for majority match.

T1.justification: The Mapper formalization, component-purity, edge-agreement, and majority-match definitions in Equations (1)–(3), and lens definitions in Appendix C are identical. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about modular prediction-aligned representations, confidence despite annotator disagreement, and Mapper's diagnostic value.

C2.justification: Interpretations of regional prediction consistency and possible overconfidence are unchanged. Both retain the same qualifications about lens sensitivity, single-dataset scope, correlational metrics, and unresolved generalization versus overfitting.

D1.justification: Implementation libraries, hyperparameters, embedding extraction instructions, and lens details are unchanged. The code-availability statement and repository link are also identical.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and positioning relative to ambiguity modeling, representation geometry, and prior topological NLP research are identical.

P1.justification: Only the arXiv margin text changes from v1 dated 20 Oct 2025 to v2 dated 29 Apr 2026. The title, authors, prose, section organization, and appendices are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12, Tables 1–7, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–24 match exactly, as does page 1 outside the updated arXiv margin stamp.

improvement.justification: The research content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information are identical, including Appendices A–L. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and its self-link produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
